headline: Coastal Access and Mountain Trail Reservations
reservation: Access to state beaches like El Matador is generally first-come, but parking is limited and requires a daily fee. Historic sites like the Adamson House require specific tour bookings. Always verify seasonal trail closures with California State Parks or the NPS before arrival.

days.title: Canyon Ruins and Coastal Piers

stops.name: Solstice Canyon
stops.detail: Hike the shaded trails to view the Roberts Ranch ruins and a perennial waterfall in the Santa Monica Mountains.

stops.name: Malibu Pier
stops.detail: Walk the historic wooden planks to observe local surfers at Surfrider Beach and take in the coastline views.

days.driving: Allow 1–2 hours; PCH traffic varies significantly by time of day
days.note: Early arrivals are recommended for Solstice Canyon parking, which fills quickly.

days.title: Mountain Peaks and Sea Stacks

stops.name: Sandstone Peak
stops.detail: Climb the highest point in the Santa Monica Mountains via the Mishe Mokwa Trail for 360-degree Pacific views.

stops.name: El Matador State Beach
stops.detail: Navigate the steep staircases to explore dramatic sea stacks, arches, and hidden caves along the shore.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for mountain transit; conditions vary on winding canyon roads
days.note: High temperatures are common inland; carry extra water for the Sandstone Peak loop.

days.title: Marine Bluffs and Wetlands

stops.name: Point Dume State Beach
stops.detail: Walk the bluff-top trails for seasonal whale watching and views of the crescent-shaped coastline.

stops.name: Malibu Lagoon State Beach
stops.detail: Stroll the boardwalks of this critical migratory bird habitat where the creek meets the ocean.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for local transfers; PCH can be congested
days.note: Whale migration typically occurs between December and April.

intel.title: Beach Lot Constraints
intel.text: Parking at El Matador and Zuma is subject to daily fees and often reaches capacity by mid-morning. Use official lots rather than restricted PCH shoulders to avoid fines.

intel.title: Canyon Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is frequently unavailable in deep canyons like Solstice or Latigo. Download offline maps and trail guides before leaving the Pacific Coast Highway.

intel.title: Coastal Fueling
intel.text: Gas stations are clustered near central Malibu and the Santa Monica border. Ensure a full tank before heading into the remote northern stretches toward Leo Carrillo.

intel.title: PCH Traffic Flow
intel.text: Commuter traffic peaks on weekdays between 7–9 AM and 4–7 PM. Plan travel outside these windows to minimize transit time between trailheads.

intel.title: Trail Safety
intel.text: Rattlesnakes are native to the Santa Monica Mountains and often sun on trails. Stay on marked paths and check for seasonal fire-related trail closures.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at LAX and drive north through Santa Monica; stock up on supplies in Malibu center before heading to canyon trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the PCH, though smaller vehicles handle narrow canyon roads more easily. Check rental agreements for off-pavement restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Malibu Pier offers a classic sunset view, though winter light shifts significantly toward the southern horizon.
